info.title: governed-bi
info.summary: Corpus browsing, relationship graphs, governed NL2SQL turns, and the turn audit log, as JSON.
info.description:
The custom REST surface `langgraph.json` mounts at the server root, beside LangGraph Server's own routes. Spec-of-record for this surface (ADR 0007, ADR 0010).

Every handler is annotated `-> dict[str, Any]`, so FastAPI neither validates nor filters a response against the schemas here: they document what the handlers build. Paths, parameters and operation ids in this file are taken from the running app.

Every route except `GET /livez` requires the shared key held in `GOVERNED_BI_API_KEY`, presented either as `x-api-key` or as `Authorization: Bearer <key>` — both spellings are read, and the value is compared in constant time (`api/auth.py`). The routes here enforce it in their own middleware (`api/routes.py`): the platform's auth wraps the routes LangGraph Server owns and not this app, so the middleware calls that module's comparison rather than a second one that could drift. `OPTIONS` is exempt, so CORS preflights are not refused for carrying no custom header.

**A server whose `GOVERNED_BI_API_KEY` is unset refuses every request with 401.** Unset never means open, and that refusal — not a wrong header — is what a first caller usually hits; the `detail` names the variable. One key is one principal, so this is transport auth and not per-user authorization.

Serving needs a live Postgres connector and a corpus; there is no offline mode.

get.description:
Process liveness. Touches neither the corpus nor the database, so it answers before the session is built. Corpus status is /audit/corpus.

The one route served without a key (`routes._OPEN_PATHS`): it returns `{"ok": true}` and nothing else, and a probe that has to hold a credential reports the credential's health instead of the process's.
What this backend can do — the UI blocks on this response and adapts its affordances to it.

401.description: No key, a key that does not match, or `GOVERNED_BI_API_KEY` unset on the server — which refuses every request. `detail` says which.

post.description:
Answer one turn, blocking. The degradation path: streaming over LangGraph Server is the primary transport, and clarification only works there.

`session_id` becomes the LangGraph thread_id, so state is server-side and rebuilt from the checkpoint, not from `history`. Threads are held in a process-local saver capped at 32; one with a pending clarification is never evicted.

A rejected request still answers 200 with `outcome: crashed` — this route reports failures in the answer shape rather than as HTTP errors.

post.description:
Answer a clarification a turn paused on, and run the turn to completion.

Refused (200, `outcome: crashed`) when `session_id` is missing, nothing is pending on that thread, `clarification_id` does not match the pending question, or the caller identity differs from the one checkpointed when the turn paused.

get.description:
Filtered, sorted, paginated assets of one type (ADR 0009 D1).

`where` repeats as `field:op:value`, split on the first two colons only, so a value may contain them. Predicates are conjunctive. A predicate that cannot be applied is returned in `unknown_where` rather than dropped. Filtering runs over the in-memory corpus, which is what retrieval runs on (ADR 0009 D5).

Sorting always tiebreaks on `id`, so a page is stable across requests.

get.description:
Every semantic-layer item touching one physical column: terms bound to it, rules on its table, FK in and out, joins whose ON clause names it, and table-grain metrics on its table.

Joins are matched by parsing the predicate, not by substring, so `id` does not match inside `customer_id`. An id that resolves to no column answers 200 with `meta.column_resolvable: false` and empty lists.

get.description:
Bounded ER view: tables as nodes, curated joins as edges (ADR 0009 D2).

`schema` and `kinds` narrow the candidate set, `focus` then walks outward over that set's edges for `radius` hops, and the budget is applied last, breadth-first from the focus — so what survives truncation is what is nearest. With no focus the budget is spent growing neighbourhoods from the best-connected node, because alphabetical order rarely holds both ends of any edge.

`boundary` and `meta` are always present. `meta.truncated` and `meta.dropped` say what was cut; a view that renders them as complete coverage is the failure this bound exists to prevent.

parameters.name: focus

parameters.description: Max nodes to return. Clamped to >= 1.

parameters.name: kinds
parameters.description: Comma-separated node kinds to keep. Every node here is a table, so this either keeps the graph or empties it.

ApiKeyHeader.name: x-api-key
ApiKeyHeader.description: The shared key held in `GOVERNED_BI_API_KEY`, compared in constant time (`api/auth.py`). This spelling is what the LangGraph SDK's own `apiKey` option sends, so the UI configures one option and `useStream` carries it too.

BearerKey.description: The same shared key, as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Not a JWT and not a session token: the presented value is compared against `GOVERNED_BI_API_KEY` itself. Read so a curl against a running server need not know which spelling the UI chose.

outcome.title: Outcome
outcome.description: register/stages.Outcome. Derived from the attempt ledger, not from whether a SQL string exists.

text.title: Text
text.description: **System copy, not the answer.** Null on the answered path and set on a refusal; answer_text is the other way round, and the client renders on that asymmetry.

answer_text.title: Answer Text
answer_text.description: The model's prose answer, from the narrate stage. Null unless outcome is answered.

failed_stage.title: Failed Stage
failed_stage.description: Which node raised, on a crashed turn: a register/stages.Stage value. A request this route itself rejects (no question, unknown session, mismatched clarification_id, identity mismatch) reports the literal "resume".

error_type.title: Error Type
error_type.description: Exception class name on a crashed turn. Never a driver message.

refused_by.title: Refused By
refused_by.description: Which control refused, keyed into register/stages.REFUSED_BY_TO_STAGE.

clarification.description: Set only when outcome is clarification; the pending ask_user interrupt.

result_table.description: Rows from the last successful query. Live only — deliberately not in `record`, so it is absent from the durable audit log. Null on every path that ran no query, which is a different fact from an empty table. Absent on a paused turn and on a request this route rejected.

audit_logged.title: Audit Logged
audit_logged.description: Whether the turn reached the durable log under runs/serve/. Absent on a paused turn and on a turn whose record carries no turn_id, because neither is logged.

audit_error.title: Audit Error
audit_error.description: ``ExceptionName: message`` from the log write. Present only when it failed; a turn that answered is not a turn that failed.

AnswerResponse.title: AnswerResponse
AnswerResponse.description:
The answer shape both chat routes return, as api/routes._shape builds it.

The eight required keys are on every reply, including a paused turn and a request the route rejects. `result_table`, `audit_logged` and `audit_error` are conditional.

schema.title: Schema
schema.description: Null on an asset kind that carries no namespace.

provenance_status.title: Provenance Status
provenance_status.description: Null means not measured, which is not the same as clean (ADR 0005 §6).

by_type.title: By Type
by_type.description: Count per asset_type, key-sorted. A type with no assets is absent.

fatal.title: Fatal
fatal.description: Problems that make the corpus unservable.

degradations.title: Degradations
degradations.description: Problems the corpus is served despite. Kept apart from `fatal` (ADR 0008 D9).

corpus_content_hash.title: Corpus Content Hash
corpus_content_hash.description: Digest of the served corpus tree. The treatment identity of any measurement taken against this server.

schemas.title: Schemas
schemas.description: Sorted distinct schema namespaces over the loaded table assets.

servable.title: Servable
servable.description: False when any fatal problem is present.

join_edges.title: Join Edges
join_edges.description: Distinct ordered table pairs carrying a join.

references.title: References
references.description: Assets that reference at least one other asset.

found.title: Found
found.description: False when no logged turn carries this turn_id. `turn_id` is then the only other key.

stages.title: Stages
stages.description: Every register field grouped by owning stage, in register/stages.Stage order; stages the register does not name sort last, alphabetically.

ledger.title: Ledger
ledger.description: `record.execution.attempts` — one row per SQL attempt. Empty when the turn attempted none.

missing_required.title: Missing Required
missing_required.description: Sorted names of required register fields this record does not carry. Judged against today's register, not the one in force when the turn was logged.

undeclared_keys.title: Undeclared Keys
undeclared_keys.description: Sorted record keys the register does not declare.

AuditTraceResponse.title: AuditTraceResponse
AuditTraceResponse.description: One logged turn, its record split by the stage that owns each field. Every key beyond `found` and `turn_id` is present only when `found` is true.

latency_sec.title: Latency Sec
latency_sec.description: Seconds, unrounded. A string when the turn recorded the quantity as not measured — the log is written with `default=str`, so a Measured lands as its rendered text.

incomplete_fields.title: Incomplete Fields
incomplete_fields.description: How many required register fields this record is missing, judged against today's register.

AuditTurnSummaryResponse.title: AuditTurnSummaryResponse
AuditTurnSummaryResponse.description: One row of the turn log. The record-sourced keys are exactly api/trace_store.SUMMARY_FIELDS: turn_id, run_id, thread_id, question_id, db_id, outcome, terminal_reason, schemas, generated_sql, latency_sec, execution.

n.title: N
n.description: Rows returned, after the limit and any thread_id filter.

log_dir.title: Log Dir
log_dir.description: Absolute path the turns were read from.

on.title: On
on.description: The join predicate. Empty when the edge declares none.

BoundaryEdgeResponse.title: BoundaryEdgeResponse
BoundaryEdgeResponse.description: A curated join leaving the scope for another namespace, as a navigable stub. One stub per (in-scope table, far table), whatever the number of joins between them.

can_edit.title: Can Edit
can_edit.description: Always false: this server has no corpus write route. The corpus is edited in its own repository through review and a pinned hash.

edit_mode.title: Edit Mode
edit_mode.description: Always "none", for the same reason as can_edit.

has_live_model.description: False when no agent model is configured; the graph still runs and refuses.

can_clarify.title: Can Clarify

checkpoint_durable.title: Checkpoint Durable
checkpoint_durable.description: False: /chat compiles with an in-process saver and LangGraph Server injects its own non-Postgres one, so no checkpoint outlives the process.

hitl_survives_process_restart.title: Hitl Survives Process Restart
hitl_survives_process_restart.description: False on both surfaces — a paused clarification is lost with the process.

CapabilitiesResponse.title: CapabilitiesResponse
CapabilitiesResponse.description: What this server can actually do. The UI blocks on it, so every key is always present.

question.title: Question
question.description: Empty or absent is answered with outcome=crashed, not 422.

session_id.title: Session Id
session_id.description: Becomes the LangGraph thread_id. Absent or empty gets a fresh random one, so a caller that omits it cannot resume a clarification.

history.title: History
history.description: Only its user entries are counted, to derive turn_index. Working memory comes from the thread's checkpoint, not from this list.

identity.title: Identity
identity.description: Caller identity a later /chat/resume must match. A string is the token; a mapping contributes its first truthy value. Absent falls back to session_id.

ChatRequest.title: ChatRequest
ChatRequest.description: The handler reads a plain JSON object and ignores keys it does not know, so nothing here is enforced by the framework: a malformed body fails inside the turn, not at validation.

session_id.description: The thread the clarification is paused on. Absent is answered with outcome=crashed.

clarification_id.title: Clarification Id
clarification_id.description: Checked against the pending question when supplied; a mismatch is refused. Omit to answer whatever is pending.

choice_id.title: Choice Id
choice_id.description: Reply by option id instead of text.

declined.title: Declined
declined.description: True resumes the turn with a declined-to-answer reply.

identity.description: Must match the identity checkpointed when the turn paused, or the resume is refused. Absent falls back to session_id.

ChatResumeRequest.title: ChatResumeRequest
ChatResumeRequest.description: Only `answer`, `choice_id` and `declined` reach the paused tool; `declined` wins, then `answer`, then `choice_id`.

question.title: Question
question.description: What the agent is asking the human.

why.title: Why

TurnRecord.title: TurnRecord
TurnRecord.description:
The turn record: exactly the 38 keys register/record.record_keys() declares, projected by serve/nodes/stamp.py — attempt_id, cache_read_tokens, cache_write_tokens, context_hash, corpus_content_hash, crossings, db_id, delivery_hash, error_type, evicted, execution, facet_channels, facet_degraded, facet_hits, failed_stage, generated_sql, guard, guardrail_errors, knobs_resolved, latency_sec, lexical_coverage, licensed, n_re_served, negative, outcome, prompt_set_hash, pulled_in, question_id, reflect_verdict, rewrite, run_id, schema_ranking, schemas, terminal_reason, thread_id, tool_delivered, turn_id, usage.

An empty object on a paused (clarification) turn and on a request a chat route rejected. A quantity the turn could not measure is an object ``{state, raw, why, relation}`` rather than a number, so `not measured` never renders as 0.
